Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, both required dogfish-policy skills, and the inherited rollout evidence. The visual-signals skill will determine what I inspect before touching the policy; the fish-control bookshelf will constrain any mechanism transfer and its notes.

The contract confirms this is a single editable Julia candidate, and the candidate must stay nonempty throughout. I’m now anchoring the images to scores, trajectories, and diagnostics; only after that will I read the bookshelf mechanisms, as its own protocol requires.

All four sampled runs are valid direct-uniform still-water evaluations, and all fail by the upper boundary. The strongest score is the half-cycle candidate; the most informative contrast is the full-quadrant redirect, which gets closest but stalls into a held bend. I’m comparing their combined top-down and oblique sheets now.

The inherited logs contain a materially stronger result than the sampled scalar ordering reveals: the prior course-angle controller reached `0.857L`, just outside the `0.75L` capture radius, before the same upper exit. I’m treating that near miss as the parent mechanism to preserve and inspecting its wake/trajectory before proposing the one new candidate.

The near miss is an active, coherent crossing—not a stall: it first enters `2L` at `17.04T`, reaches `0.857L` at `19.06T`, and is still moving at about `0.85U`. Its raw command is also actuator-limited in roughly 90% of samples, so I won’t add more peak curvature. The candidate hypothesis will preserve course-angle steering and add a tightly localized final-approach allocation that reduces oscillatory carrier demand only while closing, leaving bounded steering authority intact.

The written hypothesis now precedes the solver edit, as required. The bookshelf informed only the invariant—continuous arrival-state allocation around a stable rhythmic carrier; none of its published gains or clocked kinematics are being copied.

The candidate and both required evidence files are now complete. The durable guidance records the key inherited result: course-angle feedback cut the miss to `0.857L` despite a worse scalar score, and the supported next test is localized positive-closing allocation—not more peak gain. I’m invoking the mandated non-CFD check runner while I inspect the exact candidate and run focused edge-state checks.

The configured check-runner model is unavailable in this account, so that invocation failed before any check ran. I’m retrying the same immutable three-command protocol with a standard validation agent; the checks and no-CFD boundary remain identical.

A focused Julia probe could not start because `julia` is not on this shell’s `PATH` (no policy failure occurred). I’m locating the workspace’s Julia runtime and will still complete the Python guidance/boundary checks independently.

The guidance validator exposed a rendered-workspace defect: the same assigned parent is listed twice, so it cannot identify “exactly one” parent even though both entries are identical. I’m removing only that duplicate marker, preserving the assigned parent itself, then rerunning the mandated check.

The runtime is available under the workspace’s configured `julia-vanda` path rather than the literal `julia` command. I found it without changing the environment and am rerunning the exact contract assertions with that Julia 1.12.6 binary.

The Julia contract now passes under the configured runtime. A focused equivalence check also confirms the candidate is exactly the inherited course controller during far approach and while receding, and changes allocation only for imminent positive closing; all 17 `params.*` references resolve to returned fields.

Implemented exactly one target-policy candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1): preserves course-angle steering and adds closing-time-gated final-approach carrier relief.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1): records visual diagnosis, hypothesis, bookshelf transfer, and falsification criteria.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:53): adds the reusable `0.857L` course-angle near-miss lesson.
- Deduplicated the identical assigned-parent marker in [README.md](README.md:123), which was blocking validation.

All mandated checks pass: guidance materiality, Julia policy contract/schema, and editable-boundary audit. No CFD was run.
